text: National University of Computer & Emerging Sciences - Department of Artificial Intelligence NUCES - 11.6 Cropping import cv2 import matplotlib.pyptot as p It # Read the image = cv2.imread('Sukuna.jpegI) image # Convert from BGR to RGB for correct cotor display cv2.cvtCoUor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB) image_rgb # Get the originat image dimensions (height and width) Karachi Cropped Image (Left Half) = image_rgb . height, width # Calculate the horizontal midpoint mid_x = width // 2 # Crop the image using NumPy slicing # Syntax: image[y_start:y_end, x_start:x_end] means att rows (fult height) , :mid_x' means = image_rgb[:, :mid_x] cropped_image # Note: To keep the RIGHT half instead, use: image_rgb[:, mid_x:] # cropped _ image = # Display the cropped image intine using Matplotlib put . put . titte( 'Cropped Image (Left Half) ') ptt.axis(' off') # Hides the x and y axes columns from start to the midpoint put . show() Description : FAST NUCES - In OpenCV, images are stored as multi-dimensionat NumPy arrays, which means cropping is done using standard Python array slicing (image[y, x]) rather than a specific OpenCV function. This code first reads the image and converts it to RGB. It then retrieves the total height and width from the array's . shape property. By dividing the width by 2 (width // 2), it finds the exact vertical center line of the image. The slicing syntax image_rgb[:, :mid_x] tells the program to take att vertical rows (the full height) but only take the horizontal columns from the very left edge up to the calculated midpoint, effectively cutting off the right half of the image. Finally, the resulting cropped region is displayed intine using Matplotlib. Karachi Instructor: Talha Shahid 16
